data.content_ref: inline:The target over-narrowly requires 'Cross-Item Sensitivity' (conditional interplay between checklist items) as the only genuine reliability gain. Counterexample: a well-calibrated additive checklist on a perfectly modular task (explicitly listed as a countercondition) can yield a genuine reliability gain over a single expert's intuition because independent non-experts applying each item reduce variance and the items individually map to verifiable outcome components. By excluding modular additive checklists from 'genuine' reliability, the target falsely demotes a genuine variance-cancellation mechanism to mere compliance.
